Photo: Reuters Bucharest, July 21 (SANA) Romanian President Nicușor Dan announced on Tuesday that a Liberian-flagged vessel was subjected to an attack near Romanian territorial waters, leaving three crew members injured. Dan stated in a post on the X platform that the LPG tanker LPG Gas Lisbon was hit approximately 20 nautical miles (40 kilometers) off the Romanian coast while en route from Egypt to Ukraine . The president noted that rescue teams evacuated the ship’s crew, including the three injured members, while a tugboat was dispatched to ensure the vessel does not drift or pose a hazard to maritime navigation. Dan suggested that the strike was likely part of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war and the recent escalation witnessed in the Black Sea over recent weeks, stressing that Romanian state institutions remain on high alert to clarify the circumstances surrounding the attack. European Union officials had previously stated that Russian and Ukrainian drones repeatedly violated Romania’s airspace and territorial waters this year as part of the military escalation between the two sides. The Russia-Ukraine war escalated further at the beginning of July, with both sides shifting toward targeting economic facilities and critical infrastructure to increase mutual pressure. The national cybersecurity agency, CERT.LV, stated there is no indication of a cyberattack or external interference. by Kyiv Post | Aug. 1, 2026, 4:14 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied A member of the State Border Guard (SBG) patrols along the fence at the Latvia/Belarus border near Krivanda, Eastern Latvia on Aug. 8, 2023, during a visit by the President of Latvia. (Photo by Gints Ivuskans / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Latvia temporarily closed its border with Belarus on Friday evening, July 31, due to a technical failure at a key checkpoint, prompting authorities to redirect travelers. Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava announced the closure on social media, urging individuals seeking to return to Latvia to use alternative routes. The Latvian State Border Guard confirmed that border control operations were suspended due to information system disruptions at the Pāternieki crossing point. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . CERT.LV, Latvia’s national cybersecurity agency, reported that initial assessments showed no signs of external interference or a cyberattack. The agency attributed the disruption to localized technical issues and stated that IT specialists were assisting the border guard in resolving the situation. Advertisement The State Border Guard stated it would provide updates on the resumption of border crossings through its official channels. Heightened regional tensions The temporary closure occurs amid elevated regional security concerns along NATO’s eastern flank. In late June, Latvian intelligence officials warned that Russia might be preparing hybrid provocations – such as drone or missile incursions – against the Baltic states or Poland . The intelligence assessments suggested these potential actions would be designed to intimidate neighboring countries and pressure NATO into reducing its support for Ukraine. Officials indicated that while a conventional Russian military attack remains unlikely in the near term, the risk of miscalculation by Moscow remains a primary concern. Other Topics of Interest Poland Summons Russian Ambassador After Cruise Missile Incident A Ukrainian fighter pilot tracked the missile to the border but broke off pursuit 20 seconds before it crossed into Polish airspace. In response to regional security threats, Latvia began installing concrete anti-tank barriers along its border with Russia in May. The fortifications are part of the broader Baltic Defense Line initiative agreed upon by Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Concurrently, NATO is restructuring its command on the eastern flank to enhance regional readiness. https://www.maitlandmercury.com.au/story.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has launched a new regional grouping of eight countries from ‌the Carpathian region of central and eastern Europe at a summit ‌in Ukraine designed to promote trade and security co-operation. At the ‌meeting in western Ukraine, Zelenskiy thanked regional allies for keeping trade and transport links open following Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. The new grouping - labelled the "Carpathian Eight" - brings together Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, ‌the Czech Republic, ‌Austria, ⁠Hungary and the European Union. Polish Prime Minister ​Donald Tusk, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic and Romanian President Nicusor Dan attended the inaugural event, which is expected to last until Sunday. "This marks the start of a movement that should ⁠bring our countries even closer ‌together ​and create another strong framework for co-operation at the EU ​level," Zelenskiy ‌said on Telegram, citing the expansion of energy and ​logistics co-operation, cross-border trade and security. "Naturally, security issues are a priority right now and for the years ahead," ​Zelenskiy ​said in a ​speech. Close to 550 business representatives ‌were expected to attend the forum, with investment and trade agreements worth a billion euro ($A1.6 billion) expected to be signed, Zelenskiy said. "It's a good start: energy, logistics, infrastructure and cross-sector agreements," ​he said in a speech broadcast on Ukrainian TV. Some of the countries attending the meeting, such as Poland and Romania, have been staunch supporters of Ukraine. Others, such as Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia, have declined to provide direct military assistance to Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russia's foreign ministry said on Friday it had summoned the United Kingdom chargé d'affaires to strongly protest the UK's continued increase in the supply of drones and other weapons systems to Ukraine. The ministry said the UK's "fiercely confrontational stance" was aimed at "prolonging and escalating the armed conflict by every possible means". It added that Russia reserves the right to take necessary countermeasures in self-defence and that "any British military facilities in Ukraine used to strike Russian territory represent legitimate targets". with AP Australian Associated Press
